lead.headline: Waller in, Sadiq out: the tight-end seat changes hands a fourth time
lead.deck: You made both moves this morning: Waller for Sadiq, Downs into the flex. The lineup is now the projection lineup. Keenan Allen was ruled out today, which helps Downs. Waller's week depends on whether Jalen Coker plays.
lead.body: The tight-end seat changed hands again this morning, the fourth time in about ten days. Kenyon Sadiq went out, still only questionable and never downgraded, and Darren Waller came in as a free agent. Sadiq now sits on waivers until Wednesday, so that door is closed without spending priority. Waller is healthy and faces Detroit, who have allowed more points to tight ends than anyone. But his one productive game as a target, 8 of them, came after Jalen Coker left hurt; in the two games Coker finished, Waller drew 2 and 3. Coker is questionable again, and Carolina called up a receiver this afternoon, so Waller's role may hold. Nobody will know before 16:50 on Sunday, after every other tight end has locked. The flex is fixed: Josh Downs is in it, as the projection wanted for five editions. Keenan Allen was ruled out this afternoon with the groin injury, and Downs' 13.6 didn't move, so that is upside the number hasn't counted. Nothing else changed. No starter carries a designation, the Saints list neither Kamara nor Shough, and the Ravens D/ST hold at 7.0 without Trey Hendrickson; the Bills went to another manager this morning and the best free defence, Chicago, is half a point better. Team 13 still start DeVonta Smith and Rachaad White, both ruled out, which is why ESPN has you at 68%. That number shrinks the moment they set a lineup.
